strengths: No invented yen amounts for ご祝儀, 香典, or department-store boxes.
Ochugen/oseibo decline is framed as 2020s reporting and surveys, not a census.
Practice definitions (shareable travel food, home-visit bag, mid-year/year-end courtesy, return gifts) match ordinary usage.
Interpretation of stacked calendars is labeled; tipping is correctly a different channel.
verified: Omiyage is typically a trip souvenir, often shareable food for workplace or family—not a unique artisan object for one friend.
Temiyage is a modest item brought when visiting, especially a home.
Ochugen and oseibo are mid-year and year-end seasonal gifts historically aimed at people one is socially indebted to.
Okaeshi is a return gift after weddings, funeral incense money, or a large favor.
虚礼廃止 (kyorei haishi) is a real Japanese phrase for dropping empty formality, including seasonal gifts.
Many companies restrict or refuse gifts under compliance / anti-bribery rules.
Restaurant tipping is not the same custom as a host gift.
A first refusal of a small temiyage is often 遠慮; a hard refusal can read as rejecting the visit.
questionable: “Surveys show fewer people saying they never miss ochugen” — plausible press/Hakuhodo-style wording, but the article does not name a survey and attributes it under “department-store campaign reporting.”

Lifetime-employment decline plus tighter compliance as the explanation that seasonal accounting “looks like a leftover corporate ritual” — real pressures exist; other drivers (cost, nuclear households, time, e-gifting, COVID) are omitted and the causal tone is firmer than the evidence shown.
Classroom regional snacks after summer break — happens, but allergy rules and school policy vary; “may” is the right verb and should not harden.
needs_source: Ceremonial-market shrinkage (keep as press/market-research reporting; do not add fake percentages).
Hospital vs funeral item rules — not a citation gap so much as a merged, inaccurate rule list that should be split rather than sourced as one fact.

issues.location: What Visitors Over-Read — hospital visits and funerals
issues.problem: States a single item-rule package (flowers, incense money, no flashy wrapping) for two different institutions. That is not an accurate fact bundle. Hospital お見舞い gifts are often food or flowers; funerals center on 香典 and condolence presentation. “Do not copy omiyage logic there” overclaims for hospitals.
issues.suggestion: Untangle the two events. Do not invent yen figures or a complete 香典 table. Tell readers to ask locally.

issues.location: “So Often” Is a Cluster — surveys / 2020s reporting
issues.problem: One sentence hangs company bans, household 虚礼廃止, and “never miss ochugen” surveys on department-store campaign reporting. The hedge is present; the attribution is sloppy.
issues.suggestion: Keep hedges; say press and market surveys describe a shrinking ceremonial market. Do not invent a year, firm, or percentage.

issues.location: Why Gifts Do Social Work — Seasonal accounting
issues.problem: Employment instability and compliance are presented as the reason the twice-yearly settle-up looks leftover.
issues.suggestion: Hedge as one reason among several; do not add new statistics.
